title: Requirements Engineering Workbench Specification
description: Baseline requirements for a local, API-first Requirements Engineering Workbench aligned with IREB CPRE terminology, including development work and executable verification.

architecture.test_execution: Configured local commands executed directly by the backend with timeout and captured output

functional_requirements.title: Trace generated workflow
Run automated verification
functional_requirements.shall: execute a configured Test Case command, capture its output and exit code, and derive Passed, Failed or Blocked status

TestCase.execution_command: list of command arguments executed without a shell; empty means manual execution

api_requirements.shall: provide collection GET/POST and item GET/PUT endpoints for each managed model
return HTTP 404 when an item does not exist
prevent changing an entity ID during update
provide a Test Case execution endpoint that runs its configured command and records the execution result
apply a 60-second execution timeout and return a blocked result when the command cannot start or times out

gui_requirements.shall: serve the workbench at /gui and redirect / to /gui
display the application title, Model selector and Tooltip type selector in the first header line
not display a left-side model navigation pane
switch the displayed model when the Model selector changes
display model elements in a table
provide filtering, New and Modify controls
show validation feedback for invalid input
show action tooltips according to the selected Tooltip type
provide Work Items and Test Cases in the Model selector
provide Run and Record actions for Test Cases
display automated execution output, status and execution timestamp in Test Cases

non_functional_requirements.shall: provide direct access to model selection, filtering, creation and modification
run locally without an external database server
represent relationships through explicit references and trace links

traceability.principle: Every implemented feature should be traceable to one or more requirements.

verification.acceptance: A requirement is accepted when its specified behavior is implemented and covered by an appropriate verification test. Automated verification may execute a configured local command and records its status, output and timestamp.

use_cases.name: Maintain Requirement
use_cases.description: The requirements engineer maintains a requirement and its attributes.
use_cases.trigger: The user selects Requirements and chooses New or Modify.
postconditions: The requirement is stored and visible in the Requirements table.
main_success_scenario: System validates and persists the element
alternative_flows: The user cancels editing and no data is changed.
exception_flows: Invalid data is rejected with validation feedback.
A duplicate ID results in a conflict.
acceptance_criteria: Requirement can be created and modified

use_cases.name: Maintain Use Case
use_cases.goal: Capture system behavior as a use case
use_cases.description: The requirements engineer records actors, preconditions, flows and traceability.
use_cases.trigger: The user selects Use Cases and chooses New or Modify.
postconditions: The use case is stored with its behavioral information.
main_success_scenario: Create or modify a use case
alternative_flows: The user leaves optional flow fields empty.
acceptance_criteria: Use case contains a goal and main success scenario

use_cases.name: Trace Model Elements
use_cases.goal: Connect related requirements and model elements
use_cases.description: The stakeholder creates an explicit trace link between two model elements.
use_cases.trigger: The user selects Traceability and chooses New.
acceptance_criteria: Trace link identifies source, target and relation
